Objective: Help children recognize hibiscus, identify its calyx as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
Questions: What do you notice about the hibiscus? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.
